idiom_name: typed row class with static find and instance insert/update over pg/knex parameterised queries
implementation_notes: TypeScript's types are erased at runtime, so the gateway is a hand-written class: a static find that runs a parameterised query, maps the returned row (aliasing snake_case columns to camelCase fields) and constructs the instance, plus insert/update/delete methods that take the pool or a transaction client. Prisma and TypeORM ship different patterns - Prisma is a query/table-shaped client, TypeORM documents both Active Record (BaseEntity.save()) and Data Mapper repositories - so a gateway class is a deliberate choice for small, explicit persistence code rather than a framework feature.
pitfalls: A row fetched with a raw query is a plain object, not an instance: without explicit construction it has no methods and fails instanceof checks.
pg returns numeric and bigint columns as strings unless type parsers are set, so declared number fields can hold strings at runtime.
Mixing a hand-written gateway with an ORM (TypeORM entities, Prisma client) splits persistence across two styles and two transaction mechanisms.
Transactions require a single checked-out client; pool.query inside a BEGIN/COMMIT block silently runs on other connections.
